title: Pinning operational maturity checklist and shared responsibility
body:
PURPOSE:

This is a practical operational maturity checklist for region pin enforcement ("pinning"). The goal is to define concrete, testable milestones that move a customer from manual, ad-hoc pinning to predictable, monitored enforcement with clear SRE/SE responsibilities. It focuses on what to ship in the platform versus what customers/operators must do.

SCOPE:
- Applies to Private deployments and Dedicated installs where customers require region or zone residency guarantees.
- Covers runtime routing, storage residency assertions, telemetry, and oncall flows for pin violations.
- Does NOT cover legal contract negotiation or data classification; those live in the legal playbooks but are referenced below.

ASSUMPTIONS / CONTEXT:
- We have region identifiers at request ingress and metadata propagation through router -> serving runtime -> storage layer.
- Models can be pinned per-tenant and we can read pins synchronously at routing decision time.
- There exists a lightweight audit log emitting (pin-eval, pin-mismatch, pin-fallback).

MATURITY LEVELS (0 -> 3):

Level 0 — Observability only (ad-hoc)
- Human-maintained spreadsheets map customer -> region (source of truth outside platform).
- No automatic routing enforcement; operators perform manual checks on incidents.
- Minimal telemetry: occasional audit logs but no alerts.
- Risk: high; incidents require manual remediation.

Acceptance checklist (Level 0):
- Audit log events for pin decisions are present and stored for 30 days.
- README explaining where the canonical mapping lives (external spreadsheet).

Level 1 — Soft enforcement + alerting
- Platform evaluates region pins and tries to route accordingly but falls back automatically with a "soft-fail" event.
- Alerts trigger when fallbacks occur > threshold (e.g., 5/day/customer).
- Operator runbook for triage exists and is linked from alert.

Acceptance checklist (Level 1):
- Pin mismatch metric (per-tenant) emitted to telemetry system (count + last occurrence).
- Alert runbooks created and assigned to eng-private-deployments rota.
- Rollback and safety knobs: operator can flip per-tenant enforcement mode (soft/hard) from Console.

Level 2 — Hard enforcement with staged fallback policy
- Router enforces pin at decision time; requests that cannot satisfy pin are rejected with structured error and audit evidence.
- Customer-facing SLA language updated to reflect hard enforcement semantics.
- Automatic evidence bundling for legal/forensics on rejects.

Acceptance checklist (Level 2):
- Hard-enforcement flag available and toggleable per-tenant with audit trail.
- Rejection responses contain canonical error codes + diagnostic id (for customer support).
- Telemetry: per-customer reject ratio, per-region capacity utilization, evidence bundle generator.
- Preflight test harness to validate pinned routes before turning on hard enforcement.

Level 3 — Autonomous policy + resilience guarantees
- Smart routing can automatically rehome customers to adjacent compliant regions with documented consent path when allowed by contract.
- SLA-backed latency/capacity guarantees for pinned traffic.
- Full operator automation for remediation (e.g., staged migration job if region unavailable).

Acceptance checklist (Level 3):
- Orchestrated migration workflows for allowed exceptions with operator approval gating.
- Proof-of-residency artifacts signed and packaged for audits.
- Automated chaos tests that exercise pin enforcement and migration flows on staging clusters.

SHARED RESPONSIBILITY (high level)
- Platform (eng-private-deployments + serving-runtime):
  - Implement pin evaluation API, enforcement modes, telemetry hooks, evidence packaging.
  - Provide Console controls (toggle enforcement per-tenant) and confirm audit logging.
- SRE / Oncall:
  - Maintain alerts for fallback and reject thresholds, own first-response during incidents.
  - Run periodic incident drills that exercise pin-related runbooks and migration workflows.
- Solutions/Customer Engineering:
  - Validate customer configuration during onboarding, run preflight checks, ensure contract aligns with chosen enforcement mode.
- Legal/Compliance (consulted):
  - Approve evidence formats for external audits and retention policies.

OPERATOR RUNBOOK EXCERPTS (copy/paste friendly notes)
- Alert: PIN_MISMATCH_RATE(customer_id) > 5/day
  - Triage: check audit-log for last 20 pin-eval events for customer_id.
  - If fallbacks are from planned maintenance -> annotate incident, silence alert for scheduled window.
  - If unexplained -> escalate to eng-private-deployments lead, open JIRA with tag "pin-incident".

- Alert: PIN_REJECT_RATE(customer_id) > 1/hr (hard enforcement)
  - Triage: identify whether service capacity in pinned region is healthy (CPU/GPU/IO).
  - If region capacity healthy but routing mismatched -> roll back enforcement to soft for that tenant (Console toggle) and file detailed postmortem.

TELEMETRY & VALIDATION SIGNALS (minimum required)
- pin_eval.success_count (per-tenant, per-region)
- pin_eval.fallback_count (per-tenant, per-region)
- pin_eval.reject_count (per-tenant)
- pin_eval.last_mismatch_reason (string tag)
- evidence_bundle.id -> link to stored evidence (S3/GCS path)
- Preflight results: preflight.[customer_id].passed boolean + timestamp

Testing / Preflight plan
- Create a small test harness that runs synthetic traffic with pinned tenant headers to staging cluster. Validate:
  - Correct routing to pinned region at 99.9% for Level 2 mode.
  - Fallback semantics for overload conditions (simulate capacity pressure).
  - Evidence bundle contains request trace, routing decision, and KV cache snapshot.

Rollout staging checklist (before enabling Level 2 for customers):
- Runbook reviewed and practiced by oncall; one live drill recorded.
- Preflight harness executed for each candidate customer mapping.
- Customer engineering has signed acceptance and updated support docs.
- Legal confirmed retention window for evidence bundles.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOS
- How long do we retain evidence_bundle artifacts for enterprise customers vs standard? (Legal to confirm)
- Define canonical error codes for pin rejects (input to API team).
- Automate proof-of-residency signing (HSM vs KMS decisions).

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING ITEMS
- TODO: add sample console screenshots and API payload examples (Diego).
- TODO: wire up a lightweight Grafana dashboard prototype showing pin_reject_rate by region (Maya).
- Capture a short "playbook clip" video demonstrating operator toggling enforcement (for SOC onboarding).

REFERENCES & LINKS
- Confluence: residency-operational-maturity (see linked_artifacts above)
- GitHub: internal-runbooks PR 87 (implementation notes for evidence bundling)
- Jira: JIRA-PIN-1423 (soft->hard enforcement design doc), JIRA-PIN-1589 (telemetry schema)

END NOTES
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and ops-focused — not a legal or product spec. Use it as a checklist when preparing a customer for region pin enforcement. Expect iterations after the first two oncall drills.

Quick contact: samira@redwood-inference.internal (reach out for scheduling playbook drills)
